Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 1) Digestion of proteins begins in the:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Protein digestion starts in the stomach where pepsin breaks proteins into smaller peptides in an acidic environment.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 2) The inactive precursor of pepsin is:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Pepsinogen is secreted by chief cells and is activated to pepsin by hydrochloric acid.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 3) Hydrochloric acid in the stomach is secreted by:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Parietal cells produce hydrochloric acid, which provides the acidic pH required for pepsin activity.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 4) The enzyme that converts pepsinogen into pepsin is primarily:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Gastric acid initiates the activation of pepsinogen, and pepsin then autocatalyzes further activation.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 5) The principal enzyme responsible for protein digestion in the stomach is:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Pepsin is the major gastric proteolytic enzyme and is most active in an acidic pH.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 6) Which pancreatic enzyme digests starch?
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Pancreatic amylase hydrolyzes starch into smaller carbohydrates in the small intestine.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 7) The enzyme responsible for fat digestion is:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Pancreatic lipase hydrolyzes triglycerides into fatty acids and monoglycerides.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 8) Trypsinogen is activated by:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Enterokinase, present on the duodenal brush border, converts trypsinogen into active trypsin.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 9) The most important site of nutrient absorption is the:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: The jejunum is the primary site for absorption of carbohydrates, proteins, lipids and most vitamins.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 10) Vitamin B₁₂ is absorbed mainly in the:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: The vitamin B₁₂–intrinsic factor complex is specifically absorbed in the terminal ileum.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 11) Bile salts are essential for the absorption of:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Bile salts emulsify fats and facilitate the formation of micelles for lipid absorption.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 12) The major end product of carbohydrate digestion is:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Most dietary carbohydrates are ultimately absorbed as glucose.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 13) Fructose is absorbed from the intestine by:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Fructose enters intestinal epithelial cells through the GLUT-5 transporter.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 14) The hormone that stimulates pancreatic enzyme secretion is:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Cholecystokinin promotes secretion of enzyme-rich pancreatic juice and stimulates gallbladder contraction.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 15) Secretin primarily stimulates the pancreas to secrete:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Bicarbonate neutralizes acidic gastric contents entering the duodenum.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 16) Gastrin is secreted by:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: G cells of the gastric antrum release gastrin in response to food intake.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 17) Which hormone inhibits gastric acid secretion?
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Somatostatin suppresses the release of gastrin and directly inhibits acid secretion.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 18) The major site of iron absorption is:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Iron is absorbed predominantly in the proximal small intestine, especially the duodenum.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 19) Calcium absorption occurs mainly in the:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Calcium is absorbed chiefly in the duodenum under the influence of vitamin D.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 20) Which nutrient is absorbed directly into intestinal lymphatics?
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Long-chain fatty acids are packaged into chylomicrons and enter the lymphatic system before reaching the bloodstream.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 21) The final product of protein digestion is mainly:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Proteins are broken down into amino acids, which are absorbed across the intestinal mucosa.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 22) The enzyme located on the intestinal brush border that digests lactose is:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Lactase hydrolyzes lactose into glucose and galactose.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 23) Deficiency of lactase commonly results in:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Undigested lactose is fermented by colonic bacteria, producing bloating, abdominal cramps and diarrhea.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 24) The main site of bile salt reabsorption is:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Most bile salts are reabsorbed in the terminal ileum and returned to the liver through enterohepatic circulation.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 25) A patient develops chronic diarrhea after resection of the terminal ileum. The symptoms are primarily due to impaired absorption of vitamin B₁₂ and:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Loss of bile salt reabsorption disrupts enterohepatic circulation, leading to fat malabsorption and chronic diarrhea.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 26) The first enzyme involved in carbohydrate digestion is:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Carbohydrate digestion begins in the mouth where salivary amylase starts breaking down starch into smaller polysaccharides.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 27) The final digestion of disaccharides occurs in the:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.option4: Brush border of the small intestine
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Brush-border enzymes convert disaccharides into monosaccharides before absorption.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 28) Which monosaccharide does not require sodium-dependent transport for absorption?
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Fructose is absorbed by facilitated diffusion through GLUT-5 rather than sodium-dependent transport.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 29) Which pancreatic enzyme digests proteins?
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Trypsin is the principal pancreatic protease that hydrolyzes peptide bonds in proteins.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 30) Chymotrypsin is secreted by the pancreas as:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: It is released as an inactive zymogen and activated in the intestinal lumen by trypsin.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 31) The optimum pH for pepsin activity is:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Pepsin functions best in the highly acidic environment of the stomach.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 32) The optimum pH for pancreatic enzymes is:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Pancreatic enzymes work efficiently after gastric acid is neutralized by bicarbonate.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 33) Which hormone stimulates contraction of the gallbladder?
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Cholecystokinin promotes gallbladder contraction and the release of bile into the duodenum.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 34) Bile is produced by the:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Hepatocytes continuously produce bile, which is stored and concentrated in the gallbladder.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 35) The primary function of bile salts is to:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Emulsification increases the surface area of fat droplets, making lipid digestion more efficient.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 36) Which vitamin requires bile salts for efficient absorption?
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Fat-soluble vitamins (A, D, E and K) require normal fat absorption for efficient uptake.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 37) The major site of folic acid absorption is:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Folate is absorbed predominantly in the proximal jejunum.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 38) Most water absorption in the gastrointestinal tract occurs in the:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: The small intestine absorbs the majority of ingested water before the contents reach the colon.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 39) The principal function of the large intestine is:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: The colon concentrates feces by absorbing water and electrolytes.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 40) The end product of fat digestion before absorption is mainly:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Pancreatic lipase hydrolyzes triglycerides into monoglycerides and free fatty acids.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 41) Which lipoprotein is formed in intestinal mucosal cells after fat absorption?
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Dietary lipids are packaged into chylomicrons for transport through the lymphatic system.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 42) The immediate source of energy for most cells is:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: ATP serves as the universal energy currency for nearly all cellular activities.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 43) Glycolysis occurs in the:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: All reactions of glycolysis take place within the cytosol of the cell.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 44) The end product of glycolysis under aerobic conditions is:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Pyruvate enters mitochondria where it is converted into acetyl-CoA for further oxidation.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 45) Under anaerobic conditions, pyruvate is converted into:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Lactate formation regenerates NAD⁺, allowing glycolysis to continue in the absence of oxygen.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 46) The rate-limiting enzyme of glycolysis is:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Phosphofructokinase-1 is the key regulatory enzyme controlling the rate of glycolysis.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 47) The conversion of glucose to glycogen is known as:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Glycogenesis stores excess glucose as glycogen in the liver and skeletal muscle.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 48) Breakdown of glycogen into glucose-1-phosphate is called:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Glycogenolysis mobilizes stored glycogen during fasting or increased energy demand.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 49) Formation of glucose from non-carbohydrate precursors is known as:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Glucose is synthesized from substrates such as lactate, glycerol and glucogenic amino acids.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 50) A patient with acute pancreatitis develops bulky, foul-smelling stools that float on water. The most likely cause is deficiency of:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Inadequate lipase secretion causes fat malabsorption, resulting in steatorrhea with greasy, floating stools.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 51) The conversion of pyruvate to acetyl-CoA occurs in the:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Pyruvate enters the mitochondria and is converted to acetyl-CoA by the pyruvate dehydrogenase complex before entering the TCA cycle.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 52) The tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle occurs in the:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: The TCA cycle is the central aerobic metabolic pathway and takes place in the mitochondrial matrix.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 53) Acetyl-CoA combines with oxaloacetate to form:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Citrate is the first compound formed in the TCA cycle by condensation of acetyl-CoA with oxaloacetate.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 54) The main purpose of the TCA cycle is to:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.option2: Generate reducing equivalents for ATP synthesis
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: The TCA cycle produces NADH and FADH₂, which drive oxidative phosphorylation.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 55) The electron transport chain is located in the:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: The electron transport chain complexes are embedded in the inner mitochondrial membrane.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 56) The final electron acceptor in the electron transport chain is:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Oxygen accepts electrons and combines with hydrogen ions to form water.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 57) The major site of ATP production in aerobic metabolism is:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Most cellular ATP is generated through oxidative phosphorylation in mitochondria.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 58) The universal energy currency of the cell is:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: ATP stores and transfers energy required for cellular functions.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 59) Which hormone stimulates glycogen synthesis?
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Insulin promotes glucose uptake and glycogen synthesis in liver and skeletal muscle.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 60) Which hormone stimulates glycogen breakdown in the liver?
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Glucagon increases blood glucose by stimulating hepatic glycogenolysis.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 61) The primary storage form of carbohydrate in humans is:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Glycogen is stored mainly in the liver and skeletal muscles.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 62) Which organ stores the largest amount of glycogen?
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: The liver serves as the main glycogen reservoir for maintaining blood glucose levels.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 63) The principal storage site of triglycerides is:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Excess dietary energy is stored as triglycerides in adipose tissue.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 64) Breakdown of triglycerides into glycerol and fatty acids is called:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Lipolysis mobilizes stored fat during fasting or increased energy demand.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 65) The process of fatty acid synthesis is known as:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Lipogenesis converts excess carbohydrates into fatty acids for storage.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 66) β-oxidation of fatty acids occurs in the:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Fatty acids are broken down in mitochondria to generate acetyl-CoA and reducing equivalents.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 67) The major product of β-oxidation is:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Each cycle of β-oxidation releases acetyl-CoA, which enters the TCA cycle.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 68) Ketone bodies are synthesized mainly in the:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: During prolonged fasting or uncontrolled diabetes, the liver produces ketone bodies from acetyl-CoA.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 69) Which tissue cannot utilize ketone bodies?
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: The liver lacks the enzyme thiophorase and therefore cannot use the ketone bodies it produces.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 70) The major ketone body present in diabetic ketoacidosis is:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: β-Hydroxybutyrate is the predominant circulating ketone body in diabetic ketoacidosis.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 71) The process of glucose formation from lactate is part of the:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: In the Cori cycle, lactate produced by muscles is transported to the liver and converted back into glucose.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 72) The pentose phosphate pathway primarily produces:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: This pathway supplies NADPH for reductive biosynthesis and ribose-5-phosphate for nucleotide synthesis.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 73) The rate-limiting enzyme of the pentose phosphate pathway is:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: G6PD catalyzes the first and regulatory step of the pentose phosphate pathway.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 74) NADPH generated by the pentose phosphate pathway is essential for:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: NADPH protects cells, particularly red blood cells, against oxidative damage by regenerating reduced glutathione.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 75) A child develops fasting hypoglycemia with marked hepatomegaly due to inability to convert glucose-6-phosphate into free glucose. The most likely diagnosis is:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Glucose-6-phosphatase deficiency causes glycogen storage disease type I, characterized by severe fasting hypoglycemia, hepatomegaly, and lactic acidosis.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 76) The principal organ responsible for maintaining blood glucose during fasting is:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: The liver maintains blood glucose by glycogenolysis in early fasting and gluconeogenesis during prolonged fasting.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 77) The major substrate for gluconeogenesis during prolonged fasting is:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Alanine released from skeletal muscle is a major glucogenic amino acid used for hepatic glucose production.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 78) Which amino acid cannot be converted into glucose?
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Leucine and lysine are exclusively ketogenic amino acids and cannot serve as substrates for gluconeogenesis.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 79) The major site of the urea cycle is the:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: The liver converts toxic ammonia into urea, which is then excreted by the kidneys.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 80) The primary function of the urea cycle is to:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: The urea cycle prevents ammonia toxicity by converting it into urea.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 81) The first reaction of the urea cycle occurs in the:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Carbamoyl phosphate is formed within the mitochondrial matrix, initiating the urea cycle.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 82) Which enzyme catalyzes the rate-limiting step of the urea cycle?
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Carbamoyl phosphate synthetase I is the regulatory enzyme of the urea cycle and requires N-acetylglutamate for activation.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 83) Ammonia produced during amino acid metabolism is transported safely from tissues mainly as:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Glutamine serves as a non-toxic carrier of ammonia from peripheral tissues to the liver and kidneys.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 84) The major transport form of ammonia from skeletal muscle to the liver is:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Through the glucose-alanine cycle, muscle transfers amino groups to the liver as alanine.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 85) Which amino acid is exclusively ketogenic?
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Leucine cannot produce glucose and is metabolized only to ketogenic products.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 86) The principal nitrogenous waste product excreted in human urine is:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Urea accounts for the majority of nitrogen excreted in healthy adults.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 87) The metabolic state immediately after a carbohydrate-rich meal is characterized by increased:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Insulin promotes storage of excess glucose as glycogen during the fed state.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 88) Which hormone is the principal anabolic hormone?
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Insulin stimulates glycogen, fat and protein synthesis while inhibiting catabolic pathways.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 89) The respiratory quotient (RQ) of carbohydrate metabolism is:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Complete oxidation of carbohydrate produces equal amounts of carbon dioxide and oxygen consumption.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 90) The respiratory quotient of fat metabolism is approximately:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Fat oxidation consumes relatively more oxygen, resulting in an RQ of about 0.7.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 91) The respiratory quotient of a mixed diet is approximately:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: A typical mixed diet has an average respiratory quotient of about 0.8.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 92) The caloric value of 1 gram of carbohydrate is:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Carbohydrates yield approximately 4 kcal of energy per gram.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 93) The caloric value of 1 gram of fat is:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Fat is the most energy-dense macronutrient, providing about 9 kcal per gram.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 94) The caloric value of 1 gram of protein is:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Proteins provide approximately 4 kcal of energy per gram, although their primary role is structural and functional.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 95) Basal metabolic rate is measured under all of the following conditions except:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Exercise increases energy expenditure, so BMR must be measured under resting, post-absorptive conditions.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 96) Which factor increases basal metabolic rate the most?
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Thyroid hormones markedly increase oxygen consumption and basal metabolic rate.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 97) The specific dynamic action (thermic effect) is greatest for:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Proteins require the greatest energy expenditure for digestion, absorption and metabolism.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 98) During prolonged starvation, the brain increasingly utilizes:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Adaptation to starvation allows the brain to use ketone bodies, reducing glucose requirements.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 99) A patient with complete obstruction of the common bile duct is most likely to develop deficiency of:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Bile is essential for absorption of fat-soluble vitamins. Vitamin K deficiency can lead to impaired blood coagulation.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 100) A newborn develops persistent vomiting, lethargy and marked hyperammonemia shortly after starting protein feeding. The most likely underlying metabolic defect is:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Defects in the urea cycle impair ammonia detoxification, leading to severe neonatal hyperammonemia after protein

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 101) The irreversible step that commits glucose to glycolysis is catalyzed by:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Phosphofructokinase-1 catalyzes the committed and rate-limiting step of glycolysis and is the major regulatory point.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 102) Which metabolite allosterically activates phosphofructokinase-1?
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: AMP indicates a low-energy state and stimulates glycolysis by activating phosphofructokinase-1.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 103) Which substance inhibits phosphofructokinase-1?
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: High ATP levels signal sufficient energy, thereby inhibiting glycolysis.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 104) Pyruvate dehydrogenase requires all of the following coenzymes except:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Pyruvate dehydrogenase requires TPP, lipoic acid, CoA, FAD and NAD⁺. Biotin is not a cofactor.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 105) Which vitamin deficiency impairs pyruvate dehydrogenase activity?
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Thiamine (vitamin B₁) is essential for pyruvate dehydrogenase and α-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 106) The rate-limiting enzyme of cholesterol synthesis is:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: HMG-CoA reductase catalyzes the committed step in cholesterol biosynthesis.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 107) Statins reduce plasma cholesterol by inhibiting:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Statins competitively inhibit HMG-CoA reductase, reducing hepatic cholesterol synthesis.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 108) The rate-limiting enzyme of fatty acid synthesis is:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Acetyl-CoA carboxylase converts acetyl-CoA into malonyl-CoA, the committed step in fatty acid synthesis.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 109) Carnitine is essential for:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.option3: Transport of long-chain fatty acids into mitochondria
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Carnitine shuttles long-chain fatty acids across the inner mitochondrial membrane for β-oxidation.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 110) Malonyl-CoA inhibits:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Malonyl-CoA prevents simultaneous fatty acid synthesis and degradation by inhibiting fatty acid transport into mitochondria.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 111) The principal fuel used by red blood cells is:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Red blood cells lack mitochondria and depend entirely on anaerobic glycolysis.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 112) Which tissue depends almost exclusively on glucose under normal physiological conditions?
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Without mitochondria, red blood cells cannot oxidize fatty acids or ketone bodies.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 113) The major source of blood glucose during the first few hours of fasting is:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Hepatic glycogen breakdown maintains blood glucose during early fasting.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 114) During prolonged fasting, blood glucose is maintained mainly by:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Once liver glycogen is depleted, glucose is synthesized from non-carbohydrate precursors.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 115) Which hormone promotes lipolysis in adipose tissue?
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.option4: All of the above except insulin
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Glucagon and growth hormone promote lipolysis, whereas insulin inhibits it.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 116) The immediate precursor of ketone bodies is:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Excess acetyl-CoA generated from β-oxidation is converted into ketone bodies in the liver.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 117) Which of the following is not a ketone body?
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Pyruvate is the end product of glycolysis and is not classified as a ketone body.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 118) Which organ cannot release free glucose into the bloodstream because it lacks glucose-6-phosphatase?
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Muscle glycogen is reserved for local energy needs because skeletal muscle lacks glucose-6-phosphatase.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 119) The major metabolic function of the liver in the fed state is:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: After meals, insulin promotes hepatic uptake of glucose and glycogen formation.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 120) The major fuel used by skeletal muscle during prolonged exercise is:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: As exercise continues, skeletal muscle increasingly relies on fatty acid oxidation to conserve glycogen.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 121) Which lipoprotein transports dietary triglycerides from the intestine?
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Chylomicrons carry exogenous triglycerides from the intestine to peripheral tissues.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 122) VLDL is primarily responsible for transporting:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: VLDL is synthesized in the liver and transports endogenous triglycerides.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 123) The lipoprotein commonly known as “good cholesterol” is:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: HDL removes excess cholesterol from peripheral tissues and transports it to the liver.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 124) A patient with severe thiamine deficiency develops elevated blood lactate because pyruvate cannot be efficiently converted into:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Thiamine deficiency impairs pyruvate dehydrogenase, causing pyruvate to accumulate and be converted into lactate.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 125) A fasting patient has normal blood glucose despite depleted liver glycogen stores. Which process is primarily responsible?
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: During prolonged fasting, the liver synthesizes glucose from lactate, glycerol and glucogenic amino acids to maintain blood glucose levels.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 126) Which amino acid is exclusively glucogenic?
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Alanine is converted to pyruvate and serves as an important substrate for gluconeogenesis.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 127) The principal site of cholesterol synthesis is the:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: The liver is the major organ responsible for endogenous cholesterol synthesis.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 128) The major lipoprotein responsible for reverse cholesterol transport is:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: HDL removes excess cholesterol from peripheral tissues and transports it to the liver for disposal.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 129) During starvation, glycerol released from adipose tissue is primarily utilized for:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Glycerol is converted to dihydroxyacetone phosphate and enters the gluconeogenic pathway.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 130) The main physiological role of insulin in carbohydrate metabolism is to:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Insulin lowers blood glucose by enhancing cellular glucose uptake and promoting glycogen synthesis.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 131) The hormone-sensitive lipase present in adipose tissue is activated mainly by:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Glucagon (and catecholamines) activates hormone-sensitive lipase, increasing lipolysis during fasting.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 132) Which metabolic pathway provides glucose for tissues during prolonged fasting?
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: When glycogen stores are exhausted, glucose is synthesized from lactate, glycerol and glucogenic amino acids.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 133) A child develops severe fasting hypoglycemia with absent ketone body formation due to defective transport of long-chain fatty acids into mitochondria. The most likely deficiency is:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Carnitine is required for mitochondrial transport of long-chain fatty acids. Deficiency impairs β-oxidation and ketogenesis.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 134) An infant presents with recurrent hypoglycemia, hepatomegaly and accumulation of glycogen with normal structure. The enzyme deficiency most likely involves:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Glucose-6-phosphatase deficiency (Von Gierke disease) prevents release of free glucose from the liver, causing severe fasting hypoglycemia and hepatomegaly.

Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.question: 135) A patient with chronic alcoholism presents with ophthalmoplegia, ataxia and confusion. The underlying biochemical defect is impaired oxidative decarboxylation of pyruvate due to deficiency of:
Digestion, Absorption, Bioenergetics & M.exp: Thiamine (vitamin B₁) is an essential cofactor for pyruvate dehydrogenase. Deficiency impairs aerobic glucose metabolism and causes Wernicke encephalopathy.
